title: Penalized Cox Models and Nested Cross-Validation for Start/Stop Survival Data
text: Clinical prognostic modeling frequently involves datasets dozens continuous lab values (e.g. creatinine, bilirubin, blood pressure) alongside categorical clinical indicators (e.g. disease stage, smoking status, sex, treatment center). Standard Principal Component Analysis ([recipes::step_pca()]) operates numeric columns; dummy-encoding categorical variables PCA distorts geometric distances binary indicators different variances continuous variables. step_famd() provides native recipes step Factor Analysis Mixed Data (Pagès 2004, implemented via FactoMineR::FAMD): - Continuous variables normalized unit variance. - Categorical variables dummy-coded weighted inversely category frequencies, ensuring variable contributes proportionally regardless number levels. step_famd() integrates directly cv_coxnet() nested_cv_coxnet(), ensuring components learned strictly inside training fold without leakage.
code: library(recipes)  # Define clinical recipe with mixed numeric and categorical predictors mixed_rec <- recipe(surv ~ age + bmi + marker + treatment + site + patient_id, data = sim_data) |>   update_role(patient_id, new_role = "id") |>   # Apply FAMD to compress continuous and discrete predictors into 3 components   step_famd(age, bmi, marker, treatment, site, num_comp = 3, prefix = "FAMD_")  # Train and inspect component contributions prepped_famd <- prep(mixed_rec, training = sim_data) baked_features <- bake(prepped_famd, new_data = NULL) head(baked_features)  # Inspect variance explained by components tidy(prepped_famd, number = 1, type = "variance")

what: 4. Translating survival curves to GraphPad Prism with km_summary_to_prism()
title: Penalized Cox Models and Nested Cross-Validation for Start/Stop Survival Data
text: academic medical centers, biostatisticians frequently collaborate laboratory scientists, pharmacologists, clinical trialists require Kaplan-Meier survival data formatted GraphPad Prism manuscript figures FDA briefing documents. Prism requires unique table format: X column timepoints, separate columns per experimental group holding 1 events, 0 censored patients, NA groups. km_summary_to_prism() converts standard survival::survfit summary tables directly layout:
code: # Fit standard stratified Kaplan-Meier curve fit_km <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ treatment, data = lung) km_summary <- summary(fit_km, censored = TRUE)  km_df <- data.frame(   time     = km_summary$time,   strata   = km_summary$strata,   n.risk   = km_summary$n.risk,   n.event  = km_summary$n.event,   n.censor = km_summary$n.censor )  # Convert to GraphPad Prism layout and export to Excel prism_table <- km_summary_to_prism(   km_df,   out_xlsx = "deliverables/Prism_Survival_Table.xlsx" ) head(prism_table)

what: Integrated Standard Biostatistical and Presentation Components from Wolfson

text: New theme_cbe() theme_cbe_deck() provide minimal, publication-ready presentation-ready ggplot2 styling. New cbe_palette discrete scales scale_color_cbe() scale_fill_cbe() supply Temple Cherry complementary institutional palettes. New reporting formatters: fmt_pct(), fmt_num(), fmt_sig(), fmt_p(), fmt_hr(), words(). New cbe_cox_single() screens candidate predictors automatic proportional hazards testing (cox.zph), tidy coefficient tables explicit reference rows categorical variables, automated clinical interpretations, formatted print() method. New plot_cox_forest(), plot_cox_survival(), plot_cox_marginal() provide diagnostic survival visualizations. New child template inst/templates/template_cox_single.qmd automates univariable Cox screening sections Quarto documents. New plot_survival_km() generates standardized Kaplan-Meier survival curves using Temple Cherry styling percentage axes (supports ggsurvfit fallback). New plot_dynamic_trajectory() charts longitudinal biomarker trajectories standard errors protocol time. New plot_group_comparison() plot_missingness() build presentation-ready grouped bar charts missing data quality audits. New table_two_by_two() formats 2x2 contingency tables row percentages, margins, Fisher’s exact test p-values. New read_data_manifest(), copy_data_manifest(), validate_data_manifest(), stop_if_invalid_manifest() guarantee downstream analytical reports decks never execute stale data copies using cryptographic MD5 checksums. New validate_column_mapping(), find_section_file(), read_raw_table(), read_mapped_section_data(), summarize_section_by_time() provide schema-enforced table ingestion, duplicate column resolution, longitudinal summaries. New simulate_section_data() generates synthetic cohorts conforming mapping roles CI/testing without touching real patient data. New package_deliverables() collects rendered reports (PDF/DOCX/HTML) data deliverables across compute graph stages structured delivery ZIP archives. New audit_report_deliverables() audits source scripts referenced deliverable tokens verifies -disk existence.

text: Breaking change. glmnet_IBS() now port penalized-Cox tuning code originally meant replace, generalized column names hard-coded. previous version scored plain time/status data IPCW Brier score, treated every start/stop row independent subject, used every numeric column (including identifiers) predictor, returned IBS, lambda, alpha – none fit repeated-measures data. new signature takes rsplit, unprepped recipe (prepped inside fold), feature_names, time_data grid, id_col/start_col/stop_col/status_col, returns IBS, lambda, term, estimate, alpha (one row per coefficient lambda.min), IBS = failure_ibs (default 2) cv.glmnet() fit. censoring_weights = "none" (default) reproduces ported code: interval rows scored censoring weight 1. censoring_weights = "ipcw" scores one row per subject inverse-probability--censoring weights (Graf et al., 1999) analysis-set censoring distribution. two give different numbers; compare within one setting. New tune_over_alpha() summarize_tune_results() tune glmnet_IBS() alpha grid one split every split resample. Neither calls future::plan(). formulas, instead fit one model per candidate feature set, (given randomly drawn) alpha, add formula column. glmnet_IBS() accepts feature_names function baked analysis set, recipes whose output columns vary fold (e.g. step_pca(threshold = )). Bugs fixed relative ported code: alpha grid hard-coded 6 fixed values, produced num_alpha_values + 1 values num_fixed = 6 overwrote fixed values otherwise – now exactly num_alpha_values; outer map splits drew random alpha values workers without seed, grids reproducible – maps now run furrr_options(seed = TRUE); filling missing relative risk looped forever subject known value – now errors naming subject. internal ipcw_brier_score()/integrate_brier_score() helpers old implementation removed; scoring now goes yardstick::brier_survival_integrated().

title: TempleCBE 0.1.4
text: pca_biplot(): real PCA loadings biplot. Unlike plot_pca_bi() (draws observation arrow PC score, labeled id column), pca_biplot() draws observation scores muted point cloud overlays variable loading vectors (pca_model$rotation) labeled arrows origin – classic two-panel--one biplot. title: TempleCBE 0.1.3
text: by_column mode now respects row_order argument: row_order = FALSE (default), groups (x-axis) features (y-axis) ordered descending total missingness, matching ordering already applied default per-row/column view. Previously features stayed whatever order pivot_longer() produced (alphabetical), ignoring row_order entirely. by_column mode now auto-detects aggregated missingness effectively binary – .e. every group one contributing row (checked actual group sizes via dplyr::n(), just resulting sums) – case renders discrete “Missing”/“Present” two-level fill “Data Status” legend used default view, instead continuous black--red “# missing” gradient misleading every value 0 1 (e.g. by_column set unique subject/site id one row per group). Groups one contributing row keep existing continuous gradient, since real count meaningful (e.g. multiple readings per site time). Added fill = c("auto", "binary", "count") argument missmap() override auto-detected fill behavior explicitly needed.

title: TempleCBE 0.1.2
text: is_poisson(): chi-squared branch’s distribution.test flag inverted relative every test package (p < 0.1 mislabeled “looks Poisson”), test used statistically invalid cross-tabulation instead real goodness--fit comparison. Replaced proper chi-squared goodness--fit test using quantile-based binning fitted Poisson distribution, degrees freedom correctly reduced estimated rate. Dropped accompanying Kolmogorov-Smirnov test: KS assumes continuous null distribution, Poisson’s real point masses inflate KS statistic regardless true fit. is_normal(): switched comparing freshly simulated random sample (non-deterministic, added unnecessary noise) one-sample KS test fitted normal CDF directly. glmnet_IBS(): per-time-point Brier score normalized sum IPCW weights happened contribute, instead full test-set size — double-counted effect exclusions inflated score. Fixed follow Graf et al. (1999) IPCW estimator exactly; refactored standalone, independently-tested helpers. single_t_test(): paired = TRUE crashed unconditionally (broom::tidy() doesn’t return estimate1/estimate2 paired test) — fold-change now computed directly group vectors. Also added optional .id argument pair observations subject/record identifier instead row order, previously silently mismatched pairs unless two groups pre-sorted identically.
